cars.specification_market: European October 1974 Renault 17 Gordini production-road engine reference, type 844-12, 1605 cc, for the R1317 coupe / R1327 opening-roof programme. The earlier 1565 cc 807-12 TS, North American 807-13 and 843-13 engines, and 1774 cc 807-Ga / 807-G4 rally engines are separate specifications. No 170/200-ch racing output, prototype steering/differential, race suspension or exact gearbox/road performance is inferred. One sister-coupe programme is admitted. The later road-bodied photograph illustrates the family and its roof/louvre equipment, not a certified 1974 chassis or engine specification.
cars.summary: The Renault 17 Gordini connected a fuel-injected sporting road coupe with Renault’s factory rally-development programme, culminating in the R17’s 1974 Press on Regardless World Championship rally victory. The racing winner used a different engine: its achievement explains the family’s heritage, not the road car’s power. One original R15/R17 sister-coupe programme is counted, without adding ordinary R15s, TS/Gordini badges, roof styles, market engines, model years or racing evolutions separately.

facts.explanation: The Renault 17 Gordini connected a fuel-injected sporting road coupe with Renault’s factory rally-development programme, culminating in the R17’s 1974 Press on Regardless World Championship rally victory. The racing winner used a different engine: its achievement explains the family’s heritage, not the road car’s power. One original R15/R17 sister-coupe programme is counted, without adding ordinary R15s, TS/Gordini badges, roof styles, market engines, model years or racing evolutions separately.

cars.specification_market: European 1983 petrol Fuego Turbo introduction as described in Renault Austria’s January 27, 2009 coupe history: four cylinders, 1.6-litre class and directly stated 97 kW / 132 PS. The coefficient is a model-family historical reference, not a certified measurement of every Turbo trim. No exact displacement/engine code, gearbox, torque, weight, top speed, fuel consumption or road acceleration is inferred. Argentine naturally aspirated GTX/GTA/GTA Max engines, Berta kits and TC2000 race cars remain separate specifications; their heritage supports one Fuego family admission. Diesel record claims are excluded. The photo shows a UK road-bodied petrol Turbo, with market/equipment differences from an Austrian reference possible.
cars.summary: The Fuego combines a distinctive wind-tunnel-developed sporting coupe body with a turbocharged petrol road flagship and a major place in Argentine performance culture. Its model family became a TC2000 championship icon through the Berta/Traverso era, while the selected road reference is the European 97-kW petrol Turbo. Race cars, Argentine GTX/GTA engines, diesel records, facelifts and model years do not become additional entries or supply this road car’s mechanical figures.
